name: Ignavusaurus
sum: Ignavusaurus is a basal sauropodomorph from the Early Jurassic upper Elliot Formation of Lesotho, known from a small articulated juvenile skeleton.
wsnote: Known only from a juvenile; the holotype was about 1.5 m long and weighed about 22.5 kg (Wikipedia revision).
holotype: Not read in the sources consulted; a partial, well preserved, mostly articulated skeleton with a badly damaged skull in more than 120 fragments.
exceptional: Histology of the humerus and femur indicates a fast-growing individual perhaps under a year old.
biology: Like other early sauropodomorphs it had a long slender neck and tail.
author: Knoll 2010
